subject: ventures/birth-doula-package-pricing-calculator
professional: an experienced self-employed birth doula who keeps her own books; first checks: does the package hour count include prenatal visits, birth attendance and postpartum visits plus driving, is on-call (37-42 weeks) valued sensibly, are mileage, card fees, backup-doula pay, supplies and annual overhead all costed, is the self-employment tax treatment (Schedule SE: 15.3% on 92.35% of net earnings) right or at least disclosed, and does the 'births needed for my income goal' number reconcile with the cash per birth.

evidence.correctness: Independent Python (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/f091d3e5-eb30-514d-8285-e6f58aa0a1bf/scratchpad/doula/indep.py, no subject import, defaults retyped from the page) vs the shipped calc.mjs (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/f091d3e5-eb30-514d-8285-e6f58aa0a1bf/scratchpad/doula/probe.mjs). Matches to 1e-4: worked hours 24.8333 (4.5 visit + 14 labor + 3 admin + 3.3333 driving), net per birth $941.50 (fee 1200 - card 36 - backup 48 - mileage 87 at the IRS 2026 72.5 c/mi rate - supplies 25 - overhead 62.50), hourly $37.9128, after on-call $26.6376, fee for $40/h after on-call $1,556.81 (solving the linear equation by hand). Fails: births for the $60,000 'pre-tax income goal' is 91 because it divides by net after the notional on-call value and treats overhead as per-birth at 24 births; the cash answer with overhead as a fixed annual cost is 62 (naive cash 64). The same 'Your year' paragraph says 24 clients earn $22,596 from cash net, so 91 births would really be ~$85,700, internally inconsistent. Hours are not reduced on the 8% of births a backup attends (hourly would be $39.82, not $37.91). Core arithmetic right, one headline output wrong: 2.

evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (103 lines), index.html script (lines 131-169), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Small, pure, readable module; analyze validates negatives, >100% and births<1. Defects: index.html:136 opts() silently replaces a blank or unparsable field with the example default (blank fee becomes $1,200, confirmed with node), so analyze's 'must be a number' warnings are unreachable from the UI; the fee-for-target fixed cost re-derives mileage instead of reusing the computed line (calc.mjs:64 duplicates :53). 2.
evidence.claims: Backed: 'nothing uploaded' (page.test.mjs bans fetch/XHR/beacon; module imports only ./calc.mjs and ./usage.mjs), disclaimer and placeholders note present (index.html:58,125), Not decided section lists SE tax/deductions as accountant matters, mileage note 0.725 for 2026 matches the IRS 2026 standard business rate (72.5 c/mi), served llms.txt rewritten to marisstella.app (served-copy.mjs: no placeholder origin). Not backed: FAQ (index.html:13 and :106) says the $1,200 example has 'six hours of visits' but defaults are 4.5 h (2x1.5 + 1x1.5); 'how many births a year your income goal takes' (README, page header) returns a number that does not reconcile with the stated cash income. 2.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: a doula types her package and sees $26.64/h after on-call and a $1,557 price for $40/h, which is useful. But she cannot model the per-hour or flat overage fee the page itself recommends for births over a set length, the births-for-goal figure overstates her workload by ~45%, tax is a flat set-aside with no Schedule SE estimate, and a blanked field silently uses example numbers. Happy path works, gaps hit in the first hour: 2.
evidence.domain: Compared with standard doula practice (DONA-style package: consult, ~2 prenatal visits, on call from 37 to 42 weeks, continuous labor support, 1-2 postpartum visits, backup arrangement) and IRS Schedule SE (2025 instructions: net SE earnings x 92.35% x 15.3% up to the SS wage base). Matches: package structure, labor default 14 h, round-trip mileage at the IRS rate, backup pay averaged over missed births, overhead lines. Departs: on-call default 28 days vs the 35 days of weeks 37-42; on-call 'value' is subtracted from cash in the income-goal count; annual overhead spread over the planned births then reused for any births count; hours not reduced on backup-attended births; SE tax not computed (for the default $22,596 net it is $3,192.71, 14.13% effective, before income tax) though it is disclosed as out of scope. 2.

defects.what: Births needed for the 'yearly pre-tax income goal' divides by net after the notional on-call value and treats annual overhead as a per-birth cost at the planned 24 births: defaults give 91 births where cash reconciliation gives 62, and the same paragraph's $22,596-for-24-clients figure implies 91 births earn ~$85,700.
No test pins hourly or birthsForGoal values against a hand number; two of three seeded mutants (hourly denominator, ceil->round) survive, and the births test restates the implementation's formula.
A blank or unparsable field silently takes the example default (blank fee becomes $1,200) instead of a warning, so analyze's 'must be a number' check never fires from the page.
Worked hours are not reduced on births a backup attends, so hourly is understated (37.91 vs 39.82 at defaults) and missedBirthPct=100 still counts full labor hours.
Self-employment tax is a flat set-aside; no Schedule SE estimate (92.35% x 15.3%), though disclosed under Not decided.
FAQ (page and JSON-LD) says the $1,200 example has 'six hours of visits'; defaults give 4.5 h.
On-call default 28 days, short of the usual 37-42 week window (35 days); no overage fee for long births although the FAQ recommends one.

verdict: A tidy 103-line pure calculator whose per-birth arithmetic (hours, net, hourly, fee for target) recomputes exactly against independent Python, but its headline 'births for your income goal' is wrong by ~45% at the defaults (91 vs 62) because it subtracts a notional on-call value from a cash goal and fixes overhead per birth; tests restate formulas and let 2 of 3 seeded bugs through; blank fields silently become example values; a FAQ figure disagrees with the defaults. SE tax is not computed but is disclosed. Below the bar on correctness, verification and claims.
